title: Surrounded Regions
description:
# Surrounded Regions

Given an `m x n` matrix `board` containing `'X'` and `'O'`, capture every region of `'O'` cells that is 4-directionally surrounded by `'X'`.

A region is captured by flipping all of its `'O'` cells into `'X'`. An `'O'` must stay unchanged if it is on the border, or if it is 4-directionally connected to an `'O'` on the border. Diagonal contact does not connect regions.

Modify `board` in-place and do not return anything.

## Example 1:

**Input:** board = [["X","X","X","X"],["X","O","O","X"],["X","X","O","X"],["X","O","X","X"]]
**Output:** [["X","X","X","X"],["X","X","X","X"],["X","X","X","X"],["X","O","X","X"]]
**Explanation:** The bottom `'O'` is on the border, so it is safe. The other three `'O'` cells form one enclosed 4-directional component and are flipped.

## Example 2:

**Input:** board = [["X"]]
**Output:** [["X"]]

## Constraints:

*   `m == board.length`
*   `n == board[i].length`
*   `1 <= m, n <= 200`
*   `board[i][j]` is `'X'` or `'O'`.

solutions.name: Border DFS Marking
solutions.description:
## Approach

Only border-connected `'O'` cells are safe. Start a depth-first search from every border position, temporarily mark every reachable `'O'` as safe, then scan the whole board: remaining `'O'` cells are enclosed and become `'X'`, while safe marks are restored to `'O'`.

## Key Insight

It is easier to prove which cells must survive than to directly search for surrounded regions. Any captured region cannot touch the border through 4-directional moves.

## Complexity Analysis

Each cell is visited a constant number of times. The time complexity is `O(m * n)`, and the recursion stack can use `O(m * n)` space in the worst case.

solutions.name: Border BFS Marking
solutions.description:
## Approach

Put every border `'O'` into a queue and mark it as safe immediately. Breadth-first search then expands through 4-directional `'O'` neighbors. After the queue is empty, flip unmarked `'O'` cells and restore safe marks.

## Key Insight

This is the same border-safety idea as depth-first search, but the explicit queue avoids deep recursion on large boards and makes the frontier of safe cells visible.

## Complexity Analysis

Every cell can enter the queue at most once. The time complexity is `O(m * n)`, and the queue can hold `O(m * n)` cells.

solutions.name: Union-Find with Border Sentinel
solutions.description:
## Approach

Treat every `'O'` cell as a node in a disjoint-set structure. Union adjacent `'O'` cells, and union every border `'O'` with one sentinel node. In the final scan, flip any `'O'` whose component is not connected to the sentinel.

## Key Insight

The sentinel turns "can this component reach the border" into a constant-time connectivity query after all unions have been built.

## Complexity Analysis

The board is scanned a constant number of times. With path compression, the time complexity is `O(m * n * alpha(mn))`, and the disjoint-set arrays use `O(m * n)` space.

solutions.name: Component BFS with Border Flag
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan the board and start a breadth-first search from each unvisited `'O'`. Collect every cell in that component and record whether the component touches the border. After the component is known, flip it only when it never touched the border.

## Key Insight

This route classifies whole components directly. It is useful for teaching because the flip decision is delayed until the complete region has been inspected.

## Complexity Analysis

Each `'O'` cell is visited once, so the time complexity is `O(m * n)`. The visited array, queue, and current component list can use `O(m * n)` space.
